what: Two models, same AMD Radeon GPU, same synthesized oracles, same method: 192 independent draws per task at temperature 0.6, every candidate verified. 1,152 generations total across both models.
hardware: AMD Radeon Cloud, ROCm 7.2.1, vLLM 0.16.1, ~46 GiB device

wall_clock_cost_of_K.note: measured separately in the K-sweep; K=32 costs 1.21x the wall clock of K=1 on this GPU

findings.three_regimes_measured: rle is SATURATED (p=1.000 both models) -- verified search adds nothing. gron-5 the 32B nearly solves outright (p=0.943) -- K removes only the tail, 94.3% -> 99.99% at K=4. gron-6 is the PRODUCTIVE MIDDLE (p=0.490): a model that fails more than half the time becomes essentially certain at K=8 (99.5%) for 1.04x wall clock.
findings.the_floor_is_real: On gron-6 the 7B scored 0/192. p=0 stays 0 at every K -- 1-(1-0)^K = 0. Sampling multiplies capability; it cannot manufacture it. Both boundary conditions (p=0 and p=1) and the productive middle are now measured rather than argued.
findings.capability_gap_is_large_and_measurable: Same task, same oracle, same GPU: gron-5 p went 0.0052 -> 0.9427 (181x) and gron-6 went 0.0000 -> 0.4896 between a 7B and a 32B.
findings.practical_rule: Value of verified search is zero at p=0, near-zero at p=1, and maximal in between -- but the COST is near-zero out to K=32, so run large K always: you cannot know in advance which regime a task lands in.

raw.method: 192 i.i.d. draws per task, temperature 0.6, concurrency 32, each candidate verified against the same synthesized oracle
